title: Establish canonical component taxonomy and reconcile responsive constraints in Figma library
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Reduce runtime regressions caused by inconsistent component naming and mixed auto-layout/constraint patterns across Buttons, Table rows, and Chart primitives. Deliver a canonical taxonomy, a migration plan for existing instances, and a gated publish process that avoids large downstream breakages.

Scope:
- Canonicalize component names and variant keys for primary UI atoms (Button, IconButton, LinkButton), data rows (TableRow, TableCell), and chart wrappers (ChartFrame, ChartLegend).
- Reconcile auto-layout direction/spacing conventions (vertical vs horizontal, padding tokens).
- Normalize constraint usage (fixed width vs stretch/fill) for responsive dashboards and embed contexts.
- Create alias token layer and map legacy semantic tokens to canonical tokens to support gradual migration.

Outcomes / Acceptance criteria:
1) All affected components are in a single shared library file with documented naming conventions.
2) Variant sets use consistent ordering: state -> size -> density -> intent.
3) Auto-layout axes match component intent and do not produce unexpected size jumps when text wraps.
4) Publish includes a canary release flag; non-breaking aliases remain valid for two releases.
5) QA checklist completed and sign-off from Eng and PM.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Decision: Keep existing token names as aliases in a transitional tokens page rather than renaming them in place to avoid breaking active feature teams. (Reason: many product files reference token names directly via copy-paste.)
- Trade-off: Some deeply-nested legacy instances will be replaced via an automated script; manual review required for complex layouts. This speeds migration but requires a follow-up audit.

Migration plan (high level):
1) Export inventory of occurrences via Figma API script and tag high-risk files.
2) Implement canonical components in the library file and create alias token layer.
3) Run a staged replacement script for low-risk instances (labelled by occurrence count).
4) Manual remediation for tagged high-risk files (UX owners assigned).
5) Canary publish to a beta library and monitor errors via Console dashboard + internal Slack channel #ds-library-updates.

Rollback plan:
- If regressions detected within 48 hours of canary publish, revert the publish and run the token alias compatibility script to restore previous mappings.

Notes and links:
- Figma library (working file): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/Redwood-UI-Library-Working
- Migration script repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/tree/main/figma-migrations
- Initial inventory export: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ExampleInventory (internal)

Deliverables:
- Updated library file with canonical taxonomy and token alias page.
- Migration script with dry-run mode.
- QA checklist and sign-off log.
- Post-publish audit report template.
